research_question: Did RCEP entry change the survival path of supplier relationships already active at year-end 2017?

population.unit: Listed Chinese ticker-foreign partner supplier relationship by year
population.cohort_rule: Relationship must be active on 2017-12-31, be a foreign supplier link, and have a partner in a registered RCEP or Asian non-RCEP economy.
population.ticker_rule: Aggregate multiple valid FactSet cn_ids sharing one listed six-digit ticker. Exclude ticker 000000 and identifiers that cannot map to the verified listed-firm panel.

treatment.preferred: Country-specific annual timing: 2022 for RCEP members except Indonesia and the Philippines; 2023 for Indonesia and the Philippines; never for controls.

outcomes.primary: Absorbing survival indicator equal to one until the first year-end absence after 2017 and zero thereafter.
secondary: First-exit discrete-time hazard among relationships still at risk at the start of year t
Current FactSet active indicator allowing later reactivation
Absorbing survival with failure defined as two consecutive year-end absences
outcomes.selection_rule: The primary outcome is fixed. Secondary definitions are reported as robustness and never replace it based on significance.

estimand: Differential post-entry change in survival probability for the fixed RCEP-link cohort relative to the fixed Asian non-RCEP cohort.

estimating_equations.static: Survival_pt = alpha_p + lambda_t + beta TreatedCountryTime_ct + error_pt
estimating_equations.dynamic: Interaction-weighted event-time effects with 2021 or event time -1 omitted and never-treated Asian countries as controls.
estimating_equations.augmented: Chinese listed-firm-by-year fixed effects, if within-firm treated/control support passes the data gate.
estimating_equations.randomization_inference: Exact enumeration when feasible, otherwise 9,999 country-label assignments preserving 14 RCEP and 7 Asian-control labels; retain all draws.

identifying_assumption: Absent RCEP, the survival path of the fixed 2017 RCEP supplier-link cohort would have evolved in parallel with the fixed Asian non-RCEP cohort, conditional on relationship and common year effects.
threats: RCEP membership is not randomly assigned and member economies differ structurally from Asian controls.
Only 21 partner-country clusters are available before support exclusions.
The fixed 2017 cohort represents established relationships and does not identify effects on new links.
COVID disruptions occur during the pre-policy follow-up and may differ by country.
Year-end absence may reflect FactSet measurement rather than economic termination.

data_gate: Report pair and country counts by treatment group and year.
Require all seven registered control-country labels to be checked; absent countries are reported rather than replaced.
Report the number of relationships and survivors in every partner country and follow-up year.
Report within-Chinese-firm treated/control overlap before using firm-by-year fixed effects.
Every ticker and relationship collapse is validated and counted.
identification_gate: Plot raw survival curves and event-time estimates with 95 percent intervals.
Jointly test all available pre-treatment event coefficients.
Flag FAILED if the pre-trend test rejects at 10 percent or economically large pre-differences remain despite low power.
Run the frozen country-label randomization inference and wild cluster bootstrap.
Run leave-one-partner-country-out estimates without selecting exclusions.
evidence_gate: A positive result requires consistent sign under staged and uniform timing, a randomization-inference p-value below 0.05, and no single-country dependence.
If identification passes but the effect is ordinary under country-label assignments, mark INCONCLUSIVE.
No alternative clustering level may replace partner-country inference because it produces significance.

amendment_rule: Any post-freeze change is appended to pap/amendments.md before the changed analysis is executed.
